newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Banco do Brasil on the mend.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Banco do Brasil on the mend.

text.p: Brazil's federally owned Banco do Brasil continued to recover from recent, spectacular losses when it posted a net profit of 287.7 million reais ($263.9 million) Monday.
Officials attributed the upturn to steps to improve competitiveness taken a year ago.

That was when the bank wrote off 5.5 billion reais in long- standing bad loans and posted a 7.9 billion real, first-half loss, forcing the government to keep the bank afloat with an 8.0 billion real capital injection.
Monday's result was also up 13 percent from 255 million reais net profit in the second half of 1996.

"We have turned the page on the losses of the past," Banco do Brasil president Paulo Cesar Ximenes told a news conference. "More than just numbers, this result shows an improvement in the quality of our service."

Bad debt -- more than 60 days over maturity -- was equivalent to 10.9 percent of the bank's total credit portfolio, down from 13.3 percent in December and 17.5 percent in June last year, finance director Carlos Gilberto Caetano said.
New loans, taken out since 1996, were proving much more reliable with an overall non-payment rate of 2.7 percent, Caetano said.
He also said that, in the first half of 1997, Banco do Brasil reduced its total bad debt stockpile of about 20 billion reais by 1.0 billion through an aggressive recovery campaign.
Further contributions to the first-half result came from a 1.716 billion real profit made in financial trading, up 39.4 percent on the second half of 1996 and a 7.9 percent cut in payroll costs.

But Caetano warned against euphoria over the bank's recovery. "I've said it before and I'll say it again -- the bank is going to have steadily improving results, but do not expect any spectacular leaps forward," he said.
"The result for the first half is within our expectations. What it will be in the second half, I can't predict, but we expect the result to show a steady improvement," Caetano said.
